current_difficulty_reason: The prior Margulis occupation theorem does not provide the needed drift from tangent expansion alone under a logarithmic moment of order just above one. The authors build the logarithmic-distance function and combine a bounded-map second-order Taylor comparison with a separate large-norm moment-tail estimate, choosing the neighborhood and cutoff so both errors preserve the expansion drift. This nonlinear drift construction is the remaining nonroutine step beyond the precise prior occupation theorem; no stronger exponential-moment assumption is introduced.
